title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: discount base, multiplication by containers and rounding of the surcharge
content:
## Rule
For the hazardous-cargo surcharge written at loading under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product, the contract discount, where it applies, acts on the uplifted surcharge per container and not on the base surcharge. The amount is the per-container figure so reached multiplied by the acceptance's container count, rounded half up to the cent only on that final product, with no rounding of any intermediate figure. The product is carried exactly in cents and a half cent is rounded up to the next whole cent; the per-container figures are kept in hundredths and ten-thousandths of a dollar so that no intermediate figure is rounded. The amount is 0.00 where the light-consignment exemption applies, where the charge is not yet due, or where the acceptance already carries a hazardous-cargo surcharge row.

## Calculation order
1. Take the uplifted surcharge per container, unrounded.
2. Where the contract discount applies, reduce that uplifted figure by the discount percentage, unrounded.
3. Multiply the per-container figure by the container count.
4. Round the product half up to the cent — once, at this point only.

## Witness case (hypothetical figures)
Base surcharge 412.50 per container, total uplift 25 percent, contract discount 8 percent, 3 containers.
- Uplifted per container: 515.625, kept unrounded.
- Reduced by 8 percent of 515.625: 474.375 per container.
- Multiplied by 3: 1423.125; rounded half up once: **1423.13**.

| Reading | Figure reached | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Round the uplifted figure first (515.63), then discount (474.38), then multiply by 3 | 1423.14 | wrong — an intermediate figure was rounded |
| Take the discount on the base (8 percent of 412.50, that is 33.00) and deduct it from 515.625, then multiply by 3 | 1447.88 | wrong — the discount acts on the uplifted figure |
| Discount the uplifted figure, multiply by 3, round once | 1423.13 | correct |

## Points of judgement
- *Is the per-container figure rounded before it is multiplied?* No; only the final product is rounded.
